verdict.rationale: Better Auth's own API Key plugin lets developers create, manage, and verify API keys. Those keys support custom expiration, remaining-count/refill limits, built-in rate limiting, and user- or organization-owned keys, which bound what a credential can do. The homepage also claims "Auth for AI agents… token exchange, and agent delegation," and an MCP plugin acts as an OAuth authorization server for agent clients. However, no evidence shows per-key permission scopes or least-privilege grants, so the scoping half of the story is unproven. Missing for 10: documented per-key permission/scope restrictions, detail on agent delegation/token exchange scoping, independent or hands-on corroboration.
